sections.h2: Where does a Jackson County seller take a signed deed?
sections.html:
The signed deed goes to the county Register of Deeds at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201. Posted counter hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays, with no break at noon, and the phone line is 517-788-4350. Expect the door to be locked on legal holidays.

Most sellers never stand at the counter. A title company or closing attorney carries the deed over, pays what the office charges, and returns the stamped copy to the buyer. Still, the seller is the person who owes the transfer tax, so it helps to know what the counter will ask for.

Jackson County has 702 square miles of land, per Wikipedia, with the city of Jackson as its seat and only city. Villages include Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma and Springport, with Cement City partly inside the line. A parcel in any of those places is recorded at this same twelfth floor office.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County counter charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
One flat $30 covers each document, whatever its page count. Jackson County's statutory fee page ties that to a change on October 1, 2016, and says $4 of the $30 funds survey monument upkeep. The authority is MCL 600.2567.

The county's fee page also lists smaller items you may run into:

  • $3 added for every further instrument that one paper assigns or discharges.
  • Copies of land records at $1 a page, with $5 to certify a document.
  • Name searches starting at $5, priced at 50 cents per year covered.
  • Tax lien name searches, state or federal, at $3 each.

Payment can be cash, check or card. Checks for recording go to the Register of Deeds. If transfer tax is due, the county lets you fold it into that single check.

sections.h2: How is Jackson County transfer tax worked out?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply, 55 cents per $500 to the county and $3.75 per $500 to the state, and the Jackson County transfer tax page lists both rates. Any part of a $500 step counts as a full step. The seller is the taxpayer under MCL 207.523, and the county's share is set by MCL 207.504.

The deed itself must show the total price. A valuation affidavit can stand in for that, and it costs nothing to file, but the deed has to mention the affidavit. Write any exemption you rely on onto the deed as well.

sections.h2: Are any Jackson County transfers exempt from tax?
sections.html:
Yes, and the lists differ between the two taxes. A deed given as security, a transfer under $100, and a spouse to spouse deed that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties are exempt from both. For the state tax, a deed from an owner to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild is also exempt, and so is a deed made through a mortgage foreclosure or in place of one. See MCL 207.526.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter, so a gift to a son or daughter can escape the state tax while the county tax still applies. Phone the register of deeds with the exact deed type before the paperwork is signed.

A seller who paid on a deed that turns out to be exempt can ask the state treasury department for a refund.

sections.h2: Does my Jackson County deed need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
A deed with warranty language does. So do land contracts and assignments of land contracts that carry a warranty clause. The county treasurer must certify the tax history first, as MCL 211.135 requires for the five years before the deed's date.

Jackson County charges $5 for this certificate and wants it on a separate check payable to the Jackson County Treasurer, stapled to the recording. A quitclaim deed without warranties is excepted by the statute.

Any unpaid tax on the house will need a payoff quote from the treasurer ahead of closing, so the title company can send it from your sale proceeds.

sections.h2: What makes the Jackson County register of deeds refuse a deed?
sections.html:
The office sends back anything that breaks MCL 565.201, which the county reprints on its Recordings page. The frequent problems are layout slips and missing names:

  • Paper outside the allowed 8.5 by 11 to 8.5 by 14 inch range, or pale ink, or type smaller than 10 point.
  • Less than 2.5 inches of clear space at the head of the first page.
  • A first line that fails to name the single recordable event.
  • No printed name beneath a signature, a notary name on a different page from the notary's signature, or no grantee address.
  • No name and business address for the person who drafted it.
  • Full social security numbers left in view.

The county's FAQ adds that a photocopy cannot be recorded because only original signatures qualify. Court papers need the court seal, and a spouse's death certificate must carry the clerk's seal. Staff do not draft deeds or sell forms, so use an attorney or title agent.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about selling in Jackson County?
sections.html:
Owner occupants dominate here. QuickFacts shows 159,552 residents as of mid 2025, 69,801 housing units, and 75.0 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,377 a month on housing costs, against $557 for those without one, and median rent is $985.

  • Typical owner occupied home value, 2020 to 2024: $193,700.
  • Median household income in 2024 dollars: $66,073.
  • Share of residents 65 or older: 21.5 percent.
  • Density: roughly 228 people per square mile.

With one resident in five at retirement age, sales after a death or a move to care are common. Those sales often hinge on a clear deed history, which the county's records can confirm.

sections.h2: How can a Jackson County owner look up recorded documents?
sections.html:
The county site has a grantor and grantee name search for recorded deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous documents, and the office can set up an escrow account for people who buy many copies. You can also bring the legal description of your parcel to the counter and staff will set you up to search. A title insurance policy usually answers questions about easements or lake rights without a trip.

Property owners can sign up for the free alert that tells them when any paper is recorded under their name. That is a cheap way to notice a forged deed early.

Before talking to a buyer about a problem title, gather the recorded deed, the mortgage payoff statement and any lien notices. Those three papers answer most of what a purchaser asks.

faqs.q: Does the Jackson County recording fee go up with extra pages?
faqs.a: No. It is $30 for a document of any length. Only an extra instrument assigned or discharged on the same paper adds $3.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Jackson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. At recording the county collects 55 cents and the state $3.75 for each $500 of price, unless the deed shows a valid exemption.

faqs.q: Will Jackson County record a copy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. Only papers with original signatures are accepted. A court order needs the court's seal and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim deed in Jackson County?
faqs.a: Generally no. The certificate rule covers warranty deeds and land contracts, while quitclaim deeds without warranties are excepted. Ask your title company to check your deed.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Jackson County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., including through lunch. The office is closed on legal holidays, and the number is 517-788-4350.
